title: Graceful degradation and per-tenant rate smoothing for hosted GPU pools
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Follow-up to hosted API GPU exhaustion incident (Nov 2). This ticket implements a multi-pronged mitigation to reduce queue tail-latency and avoid total pool saturation by smoothing per-tenant ingress, introducing graceful degradation paths, and fixing autoscaler cooldown regressions discovered during the postmortem.
background: On 2025-11-02 a sustained traffic spike plus a misconfigured autoscaler cooldown caused a GPU pool to reach 100% utilization. Requests accumulated in backend queues; queue-throttling and preemptive shedding logic reacted too late causing higher 95/99 tail latency and customer errors. Our postmortem identified three contributing factors: (1) per-tenant burstiness not rate-smoothed, (2) autoscaler cooldown/scale-up threshold regression introduced in runtime-2.1, (3) insufficient per-pool observability for queue length at token-level.
timeline: 2025-11-02 10:14 incident detected -> 10:27 initial surge mitigation via manual route diversion -> 10:45 partial recovery after emergency scale-up -> 12:00 incident declared resolved. Follow-up investigation Nov 3-5; hotfix and telemetry work scheduled Nov 5-18.
root_causes: 1) Per-tenant bursts from a single high-volume customer exhausted available slots; ingress admitted full burst due to lack of smoothing. 2) Autoscaler cooldown parameter introduced in runtime-2.1 set to an aggressive value that prevented timely scale-up for the observed request pattern. 3) Queue-length alarms were coarse (per-region), lacking per-pool and per-tenant tail-latency signals.
decisions: 1) Implement a per-tenant token-based rate smoother at the admission proxy as primary mitigation. 2) Add graceful-degradation fallback: non-critical requests (low-priority) will be served by a cheaper lower-capacity pool or receive a 202+queued response with ETA. 3) Rollback the autoscaler cooldown regression in runtime-2.1 and add stricter integration tests. 4) Add per-pool queue-length and 99th-percentile token latency metrics to console and alerts.
tradeoffs: Smoothing will add small additional queuing for bursty but legitimate users (increased p50 slightly) in exchange for reducing p99 and outage risk. Fallback to cheaper pools may change end-user latency and model variant; we accept potential small quality regressions for high-reliability customers and will gate by customer tier.
implementation_summary: Phase 1 (hotfix, 2w): admission proxy rate smoother (fixed-window token-bucket per-tenant), immediate rollback patch for autoscaler cooldown, emergency runbook updates. Phase 2 (4w): graceful-degrade routing, per-pool metrics, canary and integration tests. Phase 3 (ongoing): adaptive smoothing (workload-aware), ML-based surge prediction, and documentation.

Per-pool queue_length and token_latency_99 displayed in Console for all regions and have alert thresholds configured.
Graceful-degrade routing spec approved and implemented for P1 customers behind a feature flag.
Runbook updated and team training session held; post-deployment drill executed.
